name: Bansal Roofing Products Ltd
tagline: High-ROCE, near-debt-free micro-cap PEB / roofing fabricator whose long-promised capacity ramp has now delivered (FY26 revenue +60%, PAT +90%), with fresh solar-mounting-structure optionality - a Medium-conviction 10x-optionality name still held back by commodity economics and recent margin compression
business_overview: Bansal Roofing Products designs, manufactures and installs pre-engineered building (PEB) structures, roofing and cladding systems, purlins, deck sheets, ventilators and related components, mainly for factory sheds, warehouses and showrooms, out of Gujarat (Unit II, commercialised 2021). FY26 added solar module mounting structures as a new in-house product line.
fundamentals_table: near debt-free (borrowings ~Rs 3 Cr FY26, capex via internal accruals)
Rs 154.4 Cr (+60% YoY) / ~Rs 16 Cr (10.3% margin) / Rs 10.5 Cr (+90% YoY)
PEB ~800 t/month FY24 -> ~1,200 MT/month after Phase 5 & 6 (Aug 2026), longer-term ~2,000 t/month (~Rs 200-250 Cr revenue potential)
fundamentals_narrative: One of the cleaner fundamental profiles among the legacy seeds and the ramp thesis has now started to convert: FY26 revenue rose ~60% to Rs 154 Cr and PAT ~90% to Rs 10.5 Cr, with ROCE ~34%, ROE ~28% and borrowings down to ~Rs 3 Cr, all funded by internal accruals. Phase 5 and 6 lift PEB capacity to ~1,200 MT/month by Aug 2026 (longer-term ~2,000 t/month, ~Rs 200-250 Cr revenue), and a new solar module mounting structure line was commissioned in Q1 FY27. The offset: EBITDA margin held at ~10% for FY26 but quarterly PAT margin compressed from ~9% (Q3 FY26) to ~6% (Q1 FY27) as PEB pricing power is weak and steel-linked, and Q1 FY27 revenue growth cooled to +27% YoY. The PEB / roofing space rides an infrastructure and warehousing tailwind.
technical_read: Not independently pulled; the stock broke its long ~Rs 98-135 band in FY26 and re-rated toward the ~Rs 160-165 area on the earnings step-up, so a partial re-rating has now happened.
sentiment_summary: Full thread read (topic 105356, 13 posts, Jun 2023 - Sep 2024). Positive on numbers, order wins and an aggressive hiring push, but with clear caveats: PEB is 'a tough industry with no pricing power' (comparison to Everest Industries), microcap price action runs ahead of news (the stock moved 70-80% before a Rs 9 Cr order announcement), and there is execution-history risk (the company 'overstated and underachieved' around 2018). A June 2024 concall note lays out the Unit II ramp and the Rs 200-250 Cr revenue target. Thread has been quiet for ~2 years; the FY26 delivery has since validated the ramp the trackers were waiting on.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users; no dated high-conviction call. The thread is a small group of trackers who like the quality but flag pricing power and execution as the open questions, and want Gujarat scuttlebutt on new entrants.
bse_notes: Order wins disclosed via BSE historically (e.g. a Rs 9 Cr order in Aug 2023); FY26 results filed with revenue Rs 154.4 Cr / PAT Rs 10.5 Cr and a Rs 2/share dividend; Q1 FY27 results (revenue Rs 45.9 Cr, PAT Rs 2.66 Cr) plus an earnings-call recording made available. Nothing regulatory adverse surfaced.
bull_case: The long-promised capacity ramp has begun converting - FY26 revenue +60% to Rs 154 Cr, PAT +90% to Rs 10.5 Cr - while staying near debt-free and self-funded
Rare microcap combination of high ROCE/ROE (~34%/~28%), near-zero debt and a still-reasonable (~18x) multiple
Phase 5 & 6 lift PEB capacity to ~1,200 MT/month by Aug 2026 (path to ~2,000 t/month, ~Rs 200-250 Cr revenue); new solar module mounting structure line adds a second demand vector
PEB / roofing / solar structures all ride a structural infra + warehousing + renewables capex tailwind
Real, disclosed order wins and a maiden/continuing dividend
bear_case: PEB fabrication has weak, steel-linked pricing power; quarterly PAT margin already compressed from ~9% (Q3 FY26) to ~6% (Q1 FY27) and new Gujarat entrants can compress further
Execution-history risk - the company has a past of over-promising and under-delivering (circa 2018)
Thinly traded microcap where the price has historically front-run news; demand is cyclical and capex-linked
On the stated ~Rs 200-250 Cr revenue ceiling the business is a 2-3x compounder, not an obvious 10x, unless solar structures / value-added mix scale well beyond guidance
No fresh community conviction and the thread has been silent ~2 years
verdict_headline: High-quality, still-reasonably-priced microcap whose capacity ramp has started delivering - a Medium-conviction 10x-optionality name, capped by commodity economics and recent margin compression
verdict_reasoning: Legacy-108-screen seed (old bucket Tier A 'genuinely promising growth-with-quality microcap'). The deep read upgrades it: the FY26 print (revenue +60%, PAT +90%, ROCE ~34%, near debt-free) confirms the capacity ramp that was 'unconfirmed' a year ago, and a new solar-mounting-structure line adds optionality - so conviction moves Low-Medium -> Medium

four_box scores 2.0 (tailwind yes; tam weak - stated capacity caps revenue near Rs 250 Cr, a 2-3x not a clean 10x; moat no - weak PEB pricing power; valuation weak - re-rated to ~18x with margins compressing). Written exception per the decision table: growth is un-ignorable (phreak's carve-out) and this is a live small-cap inflection, so the '10x-in-2-3-years' label is retained but conviction is capped at Medium with an 'unconfirmed beyond guidance' caveat
The 10x still needs solar structures / VAP mix to scale well past the stated PEB revenue ceiling AND margins to hold despite limited pricing power - hence Medium, not higher
No red-flag tier. Worth re-checking on the Phase 5/6 commissioning update, the solar-structure ramp, and whether Q2-Q3 FY27 margins recover

New product segment: solar module mounting structures, machinery installed and operational in Q1 FY27
~Rs 5 Cr machinery capex in Q1 FY27 (high-speed roll-forming machines, CNC plasma cutting); Phase 5 & 6 expansions under construction, ~half of Phase 6 operationalised for light fabrication
key_new_facts: The capacity ramp that was 'unconfirmed' at the last review has delivered - FY26 revenue +60%, PAT +90%, off internal accruals with debt still ~Rs 3 Cr
PEB capacity guided to ~1,200 MT/month by Aug 2026 (Phase 5 & 6), a more concrete near-term number than the older 800->2,000 t/month framing
Solar module mounting structures is a genuinely new, commissioned product line - a second demand vector beyond PEB
Quarterly PAT margin has compressed (~9% -> ~6% over three quarters), confirming the thread's weak-pricing-power concern in the numbers
Stock has re-rated out of its multi-year Rs 98-135 band to ~Rs 160-165; P/E ~18x, mcap ~Rs 200 Cr
open_questions: Do Q2-Q3 FY27 margins recover, or is ~6% PAT margin the new normal as competition and steel pass-through bite?
How large can solar module mounting structures realistically get, and at what margin vs PEB?
Is the ~Rs 200-250 Cr stated revenue ceiling a hard cap, or does management raise the capacity/target again once Phase 5/6 stabilise?
Any repeat of the 2018 over-promise/under-deliver pattern as the build-out compounds?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Low-Medium -> Medium. FY26 delivered the long-promised ramp (revenue +60%, PAT +90%) while staying near debt-free at ~34% ROCE, and a new solar-structure line adds optionality; but weak PEB pricing power (visible in the ~9%->~6% quarterly PAT-margin slide), a capacity-bound revenue ceiling and a stock that has already partly re-rated cap it at Medium.
